body.statement: Is the uniform excess-endpoint rate \(\{\log n/n\}^{\beta/(2\beta+2)}+n^{-1/2}\) minimax, up to logarithmic factors, over \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) when baseline-conditional quasi-stayer support can approach failure and \(R(P)\) can approach zero? More sharply, can a matching lower bound distinguish the cost of learning the obstacle boundary from the cost of the signed objective as the identified set changes from a singleton to an interval?
body.justification: The upper rate becomes economically interpretable only after separating unavoidable support-hole learning from avoidable conservatism in the outer program.
body.gap: Slow-mover limit theory retains point identification, while calibrated partial-identification inference fixes the identified-set topology; neither supplies a minimax lower bound across this point-to-set transition.
body.consumer: A matching lower bound would tell practitioners whether shorter uniformly honest WAOSS intervals require stronger support information rather than a different optimizer.

obligation.what_is_open: A matching minimax lower bound, uniform through \(R(P)\to0\), that separately attributes endpoint loss to learning the obstacle boundary and to learning the signed objective.
obligation.obstruction: The fixed regular-class assumptions give the upper-band ingredients but do not furnish a least-favorable family. The suggested shrinking-hole handle is not itself a proof of membership in the fixed known finite-rectangle support class, bounded Kullback--Leibler divergence, or optimized-endpoint separation.
obligation.attempted: The natural two-point route perturbs \(g\) by a local \(\beta\)-H\"older bump and changes the signed baseline mass. Keeping the known support and density bounds fixed while proving both legal-completion compatibility and a nonvanishing separation of the optimized endpoints requires an additional construction; assuming those properties would assume the crux.
obligation.partial_result: The proved upper bound is uniform and equals \(O(\{\log n/n\}^{\beta/(2\beta+2)}+n^{-1/2})\).  The frozen primitives do not provide a pair or hypercube of laws in the fixed known-support class whose Kullback--Leibler divergences and optimized-endpoint separations establish a matching lower bound, nor do they prove separate lower bounds for obstacle learning and signed-objective learning as \(R(P)\to0\).
